rules.title: Schedules, statements and other documents due
rules.quoted_text: Unless (d), (e), (f), or (h) provides otherwise, the debtor in a voluntary case must file the documents required by (b)(1), (b)(4), (b)(5), and (b)(6) with the petition or within 14 days after it is filed.
rules.description: Rule 1007(c)(1): the schedules (B106A–J, B106Sum, B106Dec), the statement of financial affairs (B107), the statement of intention (B108), the means-test forms (B122) and the payment advices are due with the petition or within 14 days after it is filed. Dismiss this deadline if everything was filed with the petition.

rules.title: § 521(b) credit-counseling certificate due
rules.quoted_text: In a voluntary case, the documents required by (b)(3)(A), (C), or (D) must be filed with the petition. Unless the court orders otherwise, a debtor who has filed a statement under (b)(3)(B) must file the documents required by (b)(3)(A) within 14 days after the order for relief is entered.
rules.description: Rule 1007(c)(3): a debtor who filed only the (b)(3)(B) statement — the briefing was received, but the § 521(b) certificate was not yet in hand — must file the certificate (and any debt-repayment plan) within 14 days after the order for relief. Dismiss this deadline if the certificate was filed with the petition.

rules.title: Chapter 13 plan due
rules.quoted_text: The debtor must file a Chapter 13 plan with the petition or within 14 days after the petition is filed.
rules.description: Rule 3015(b)(1): the Chapter 13 plan is due with the petition or within 14 days after it is filed. Dismiss this deadline if the plan was filed with the petition.

rules.title: § 341 meeting of creditors — window the court schedules in
rules.quoted_text: in a Chapter 7 or 11 case, no fewer than 21 days and no more than 40 days after the order for relief
rules.description: Rule 2003(a)(1)(A): the United States trustee must call the § 341(a) meeting no fewer than 21 and no more than 40 days after the order for relief. This is the window, not the date — record the date the court sets on the case and this window is replaced by the meeting itself.

rules.title: § 341 meeting of creditors — window the court schedules in
rules.quoted_text: in a Chapter 12 case, no fewer than 21 days and no more than 35 days after the order for relief
rules.description: Rule 2003(a)(1)(B): in a Chapter 12 case the § 341(a) meeting is called no fewer than 21 and no more than 35 days after the order for relief. This is the window, not the date — record the date the court sets on the case and this window is replaced by the meeting itself.

rules.title: § 341 meeting of creditors — window the court schedules in
rules.quoted_text: in a Chapter 13 case, no fewer than 21 days and no more than 50 days after the order for relief
rules.description: Rule 2003(a)(1)(C): in a Chapter 13 case the § 341(a) meeting is called no fewer than 21 and no more than 50 days after the order for relief. This is the window, not the date — record the date the court sets on the case and this window is replaced by the meeting itself.

rules.title: § 341 meeting of creditors
rules.quoted_text: Within a reasonable time after the order for relief in a case under this title, the United States trustee shall convene and preside at a meeting of creditors.
rules.description: The first date the court set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors — the anchor Rules 4004(a), 4007(c), 4008(a) and 1007(c)(4) count from. The time and place are on the court's notice (Form 309); this entry carries the date alone.

rules.title: Statement of intention (Form 108) due
rules.quoted_text: within thirty days after the date of the filing of a petition under chapter 7 of this title or on or before the date of the meeting of creditors, whichever is earlier, or within such additional time as the court, for cause, within such period fixes, file with the clerk a statement of his intention with respect to the retention or surrender of such property
rules.description: § 521(a)(2)(A): an individual Chapter 7 debtor whose schedules list debts secured by property of the estate must file the statement of intention within 30 days after the petition or on or before the § 341 meeting date, whichever is earlier. Generated at the earlier of the two once the meeting date is known.

rules.title: Perform the statement of intention
rules.quoted_text: within 30 days after the first date set for the meeting of creditors under section 341(a), or within such additional time as the court, for cause, within such 30-day period fixes, perform his intention with respect to such property
rules.description: § 521(a)(2)(B): the Chapter 7 debtor must perform the stated intention — surrender, redeem, or reaffirm — within 30 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting, unless the court extends the time within that period.

rules.title: First Chapter 13 plan payment due
rules.quoted_text: the debtor shall commence making payments not later than 30 days after the date of the filing of the plan or the order for relief, whichever is earlier
rules.description: § 1326(a)(1): the Chapter 13 debtor must commence plan payments not later than 30 days after the order for relief or the filing of the plan, whichever is earlier — the order for relief is the petition date in a voluntary case, and a plan filed with or after the petition never moves this earlier.

rules.title: Deadline to object to the debtor's discharge
rules.quoted_text: In a Chapter 7 case, a complaint—or a motion under § 727(a)(8) or (9)—objecting to a discharge must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors. [...] In a Chapter 13 case, a motion objecting to a discharge under § 1328(f) must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors.
rules.description: Rule 4004(a): a complaint (or § 727(a)(8)/(9) motion) objecting to a Chapter 7 discharge, or a motion objecting to a Chapter 13 discharge under § 1328(f), must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting. In a Chapter 11 case the deadline is the first date set for the confirmation hearing, which this case does not record.

rules.title: Deadline for § 523(c) dischargeability complaints
rules.quoted_text: a complaint to determine whether a debt is dischargeable under § 523(c) must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors.
rules.description: Rule 4007(c): a complaint to determine the dischargeability of a debt under § 523(c) — fraud, fiduciary defalcation, willful and malicious injury — must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting. Rule 4007(d)'s hardship-discharge variant in Chapter 13 is set by the court on motion and is not generated.

rules.title: Reaffirmation agreements due
rules.quoted_text: A reaffirmation agreement must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting of creditors.
rules.description: Rule 4008(a): a reaffirmation agreement must be filed within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341(a) meeting. The rule is chapter-neutral; it is generated for Chapter 7, where reaffirming a secured debt is the ordinary course — dismiss it when nothing is being reaffirmed.

rules.title: Financial-management course certificate due
rules.quoted_text: in a Chapter 7 case, within 60 days after the first date set for the meeting of creditors under § 341
rules.description: Rule 1007(c)(4): in a Chapter 7 case the certificate of completion of the personal financial-management course required by (b)(7) is due within 60 days after the first date set for the § 341 meeting, unless the approved provider has notified the court directly. In Chapter 11 and 13 cases it is due no later than the last plan payment (or a § 1141(d)(5)(B)/§ 1328(b) motion), which this case does not record.

rules.title: Proofs of claim due (non-governmental creditors)
rules.quoted_text: In a voluntary Chapter 7 case or in a Chapter 12 or 13 case, the proof of claim is timely if filed within 70 days after the order for relief or entry of an order converting the case to Chapter 12 or 13.
rules.description: Rule 3002(c): in a voluntary Chapter 7, 12 or 13 case a non-governmental creditor's proof of claim is timely if filed within 70 days after the order for relief. The exceptions in (c)(1)–(7) — governmental units, infants and incompetents, judgments, rejected contracts, foreign-address creditors, and mortgage claims — have their own periods.

rules.title: Proofs of claim due (governmental units)
rules.quoted_text: A governmental unit's proof of claim is timely if filed within 180 days after the order for relief.
rules.description: Rule 3002(c)(1): a governmental unit's proof of claim is timely if filed within 180 days after the order for relief; a claim resulting from a tax return filed under § 1308 has a further period this entry does not carry.
